findings.title: Later complete write mismatch bypasses protocol validation
findings.observation: The replicated write payload check is inside the earliest successful receipt selection branch. Once an earlier correct completion has been collected, a later complete/admitted reply with a different write value is retained as complete and returns nil. Reversed collection instead reports an error when the mismatched later reply is collected first.
findings.source_status: conditional verified in exact frozen source; no actual independent overlay runtime control yet
findings.implication: The collector may report a normal history while a retained write reply violates the API contract that retries return the original replicated result. This is an existing validation gap, not evidence that the frozen native runs exhibited a wrong value.
findings.proposed_minimum: Validate every complete write response against the request payload before selecting the earliest completion, while preserving attempts, uncertainty, and error propagation.

NR_001_resolution.code: Every complete write reply is compared with the logical request payload after its attempt and possible admission are retained, before any earliest-receipt selection. A conflicting completion returns the existing protocol error and cannot establish or replace logical completion.
NR_001_resolution.runtime: The same independent HTTP test and overlay bytes that previously failed now pass both collection orders. Physical-source added regression also passes both orders, explicitly checking conflicting attempt retention, unchanged previous completion/value, possible admission, and no invented completion when wrong response is collected first.
NR_001_resolution.delta_from_candidate_02: Exactly the existing write-value validation guard moved outside earliest-receipt selection; API and the three receipt scheduling controls remain byte-identical. One separate physical-source regression file was added.
NR_001_resolution.retained_native_wrong_value_claim: NONE; the conflicting reply control is an explicitly synthetic protocol peer sharing parent PID and earns no distributed-target credit.
